records.title: A travelling-wave strategy for plant–fungal trade
records.software_license: MIT (analysis code, as stated by the paper)

data_rights.notes: Paper states main-analysis and figure source data are on Figshare and analysis code is MIT. Record the data artifact's own license and any third-party restrictions per file before redistribution.

records.published_sample_summary: Three arbuscular-mycorrhizal fungal strains were studied: Rhizophagus irregularis A5 (DAOM664344), R. irregularis C2 (DAOM664346), and Rhizophagus aggregatum. A typical longitudinal network experiment acquired about 150 stitched-field images per replicate at 2-hour intervals in a split Petri plate that constrained the growing extraradical network to a 2D imaging plane. The paper reports tracking more than 500,000 fungal nodes across replicates (about 40,000 nodes per plate) and mapping approximately 100,000 bidirectional cytoplasmic-flow trajectories to coordinates in the evolving graph. The flow analysis used more than 1,600 high-magnification videos from 28 biological samples/plates, typically 20–25 frames/s for 20–60 s and 20–100 sampled positions per plate. The article reports rich within-hypha bidirectional and antiparallel streams, velocity variation across time/space, and direction switching. The paper provides source data for main analyses/figures at Figshare; the associated code README says the archive includes figure source data and a subsample of raw data to demonstrate the pipeline, not necessarily the full original microscopy/video acquisition archive.
benchmark_tasks: hyphal edge identity and temporal graph reconstruction
tip, branch, junction and anastomosis event detection
traveling-wave front position and speed prediction
spatial filament-density and growing-tip-density profile prediction
antiparallel stream detection within a single hypha
flow direction and velocity distribution prediction
cost-efficiency position relative to minimum-spanning-tree and Delaunay-triangulation limits
robustness and route-shortcut changes after observed anastomosis
strain, host-status and treatment transfer where source metadata support a clean split
records.independent_unit: Biological fungal network / split-Petri-plate replicate is the primary grouping unit. The >100,000 trajectories, image frames, tracked nodes, edges and sampled positions are nested measurements, not independent biological replicates. Strain is a separate transfer/domain axis: within-strain replicate-disjoint generalization and leave-one-strain-out transfer must be reported independently. Exact plate, strain, host status, treatment, timepoint and flow-video joins must be recovered from source metadata before splitting.
split_requirements: Recover exact Figshare file, plate/network, biological replicate, strain, host status, treatment, timepoint, image and flow-video mappings before assigning splits.
Keep every timepoint, frame, node track, edge track, image crop, flow video and particle trajectory from one biological network/plate in one partition.
Use replicate/network-disjoint splits for within-strain generalization.
Report leave-one-strain-out transfer separately across R. irregularis A5, R. irregularis C2 and R. aggregatum; three strains are too few to claim broad cross-species generality.
Do not treat 100,000 trajectories or 500,000 nodes as the statistical sample size; uncertainty must cluster at the independent network/plate level.
Preserve the difference between 2D split-plate imaging geometry and 3D soil-network topology; no unqualified 3D ground truth claim.
Preserve trajectory direction, simultaneous antiparallel streams, track censoring and the 10-frame minimum trajectory rule used by the source pipeline; re-evaluate short-trajectory bias separately.
Separate source-data reproductions from any new test subset; do not use published figure-source data for both model tuning and final held-out scoring.
Freeze all preprocessing, segmentation, tracking and kymograph thresholds using training/development networks only.
known_limitations: The extraradical network was constrained to a two-dimensional split-Petri-plate imaging plane; it is not complete three-dimensional soil-network ground truth.
The paper describes over 1,600 high-magnification flow videos from 28 biological samples/plates, with multiple positions and trajectories nested within each biological sample.
The high-magnification bright-field flow observations are label-free contrast-particle trajectories; they are not direct isotope delivery measurements or a complete mass-flux measurement.
The paper's flow analysis excludes tracks shorter than ten consecutive frames, creating a documented detection window and possible short-event selection bias that should be measured.
Manual review was used to validate detected kymograph trajectories; exact annotator-level agreement and full inter-rater reliability are not established by the paper alone.

The Figshare archive and code README distinguish source data for figure reproduction from a subsample of raw data that demonstrates the pipeline; do not assume the entire original microscope image/video archive is included.

The code repository is a frozen publication-reproducibility version and documents external setup dependencies (including Fiji for stitching and anisotropic filtering for the optimal skeleton segmentation path); a clean modern environment must be created for fair computational benchmarking.
The paper's graph efficiency comparison uses minimum-spanning-tree and Delaunay-triangulation limiting networks; it does not establish that either is a sufficient functional transport model.
Results from three AM fungal strains do not justify a species-general fungal growth or cytoplasmic-flow model.
source_manifest_requirements: Figshare article version, file manifest, per-file SHA-256/BLAKE3 and per-file data license
Exact frozen AMFTravellingWave Git commit and MIT license copy
2-hour imaging schedule, image stitching transforms, pixel size and coordinate frame
Per-video acquisition coordinates, objective magnification, frame rate, duration and ROI-to-network registration
Raw/processed kymograph provenance, KymoButler version/checkpoint and trajectory filtering thresholds
Manual flow-review and trajectory adjudication protocol
Network edge/node identity tracking and graph extraction parameter history
Clear distinction between data needed for figure reproduction and any subset of raw demonstration data
recommended_baselines: Frozen AMFTravellingWave / AMFTrack published pipeline and figure-source outputs
Persistence of previous graph and previous flow velocity
BARE travelling-wave model used/extended in the source paper
Minimum-spanning-tree and Delaunay-triangulation limiting graph references
Independent flow-speed distribution and directional histogram baselines
Shuffled trajectory-to-edge registration and reversed-time negative controls

records.title: SkelPy — fungal skeletonization software and example images
records.software_license: Repository license must be checked at the exact code commit; do not assume the article's CC BY-NC 4.0 license applies to the code or example images.

data_rights.notes: The paper states that the SkelPy repository contains source code and example images. The full 180-image time series is not stated as publicly available. Check the GitHub repository's code and example-image license separately; article CC BY-NC terms do not automatically apply to repository contents.

records.published_sample_summary: Three Botrytis cinerea isolates (KatieTomato, B05.10 and 1.04.25) were grown in a 96-well plate in triplicate and imaged at 4-hour intervals over 72 hours, yielding 180 2D bottom-plane time-series images (20 timepoints). The paper also reports a separate throughput run on 3,842 images. Manual skeleton-overlay comparison used 15 images from isolate 1.04.25: mean nearest-skeleton distance 0.0046 image-width units (SD 0.0009; maximum 0.0195). Node precision was 80.8% on 30 images against a cleaned network generated by the SkelPy preprocessing workflow. A separate 30-cell spatial presence/absence sample reported F1=0.905 (accuracy 86.2%, sensitivity 90.5%, specificity 75.0%, precision 90.5%). Trait checks reported LinesInImage versus manual hyphal-length estimate r=0.99 and fractal dimension versus gridline colonization r=0.81. Processing 180 images took 102 minutes and 234 MB on an Apple M4 MacBook Pro; a separate 3,842-image run took 12.5 hours.
benchmark_tasks: node precision / recall with independently adjudicated references
hyphal length and segment-count trait agreement
records.independent_unit: Well / biological culture replicate; all 20 timepoints from a well must remain in one partition. Recover exact well-to-isolate and replicate mapping before splitting. Leave-isolate-out is a separate domain-transfer test, not a substitute for replicate-disjoint evaluation.
split_requirements: Recover the exact well, culture-replicate, isolate and timepoint mapping before assigning splits; do not infer biological units solely from image filenames.
Keep all 20 timepoints from one well/culture series in one partition.
Use well/culture replicate-disjoint evaluation for within-study generalization and leave-isolate-out evaluation as a distinct domain-transfer task.

The paper states that default preprocessing and skeletonization parameters were empirically optimized on all 180 study images; a new benchmark must freeze parameters using training/development data only and reserve a genuinely untouched test set.
Separate the 15-image manual skeleton-distance comparison, 30-image node-reference validation and 30-cell presence/absence validation; they are different metrics and samples.
Do not compare the 30-cell presence/absence F1 directly with filament detection or crossing-detection F1 from Sten or another task.
Do not treat the cleaned SkelPyR network as independent ground truth for the 30-image node check; it is generated by the same SkelPy preprocessing workflow.
known_limitations: The plate reader imaged the bottom focal plane; the source images are 2D projections and do not establish complete 3D network truth.
The manual skeleton-overlay validation covers only 15 images from isolate 1.04.25, not all three isolates or all 180 images.

The reported node precision of 80.8% on 30 images uses cleaned SkelPyR networks from the SkelPy preprocessing workflow as the reference; it is not an independent biological ground-truth annotation set.

The separate presence/absence F1 of 0.905 is based on 30 sampled spatial cells and a single user recording node presence and SkelPy prediction; uncertainty and inter-rater agreement are not established by that sample.
Default preprocessing/skeletonization parameters were empirically optimized on the same 180-image study dataset; the published result is not a parameter-frozen external holdout benchmark.
The full 180-image raw time series and separate 3,842-image throughput series are not identified as public downloads; the article's data statement lists source code and example images.
The article is CC BY-NC 4.0, but that does not automatically establish the separate GitHub repository code/example-image license or rights for unpublished/raw images.
Reported width is a morphology-derived proxy for transport efficacy, not a direct measurement of conductance or nutrient flux.
source_manifest_requirements: Exact Git commits for SkelPy and downstream R analysis
Per-file code/example image digests and licenses
Imaging plane, scale and calibration metadata
Preprocessing parameter history and explicit train/dev/test tuning boundaries

Author permission for the full raw image series and throughput dataset if requested

records.title: The mycelial network organization adapts to facilitate new substrate colonization and fruiting in Agaricus bisporus

data_rights.license_label: Article: CC BY (Utrecht University research portal)
data_rights.notes: The article is listed as CC BY by the Utrecht University research portal. Confirm the raw Figshare record's own license, file-level terms and any third-party image/metadata rights before reuse or redistribution.

records.published_sample_summary: Longitudinal Agaricus bisporus imaging with a directional new-substrate assay (six biological replicates per treatment) and a separate horizontal-box fructification time series (three independent cultivation cycles, two flushes each). Optical grayscale intensity is a colonization proxy; cord abundance is quantified by surface area; cord widening was observed near expanding primordia. Cord abundance varied substantially between cultivation cycles, and the study reported no significant correlation between cord formation and total mushroom yield.
benchmark_tasks: cross-validation against independent isotope source-to-sink outcomes
records.independent_unit: For the directional-growth assay, preserve biological replicate/treatment groups. For the horizontal-box longitudinal series, preserve the cultivation cycle/box and all timepoints/flushes. Resolve exact file-level IDs from raw Figshare metadata before split assignment.
split_requirements: Keep all scans, frames, substrate regions, repeated measures and flushes from one biological replicate/cultivation box/cycle in one split.
Use leave-one-independent-cultivation-cycle-out evaluation for the three-cycle longitudinal fructification series; report wide uncertainty and avoid overclaiming from n=3 cycles.
Keep the six-replicate directional-growth experiment separate from the three-cycle longitudinal cultivation experiment; do not treat them as one shared cohort.
Use leave-treatment-out tests for directional new-substrate conditions and leave-cycle-out tests for fructification dynamics.
Keep isotope transfer outcomes as a separate dataset/task; join only if source files establish a genuine shared experimental unit or paired experiment.
known_limitations: Grayscale intensity is a colonization proxy, not a direct measurement of fungal biomass.
Cord area and width are structural measurements, not direct conductance or flux observations.
The longitudinal fructification study comprised three independent cultivation cycles and reported substantial between-cycle variation in cord-formation timing and magnitude.
The authors found no significant correlation between cord formation and total mushroom yield; cord abundance must not be used as a general yield proxy.
Water availability may constrain cord formation, especially near the casing layer; hydration is a potential moderator.
The reported association between new-substrate extension, developing primordia and cord formation does not establish a causal effect.
Raw Figshare terms and exact sample/replicate IDs must be verified before ingestion.
source_manifest_requirements: Figshare record/version and per-file content digests
Image acquisition timepoint and stage labels
Spatial calibration, scale and coordinate transforms
Analysis code/version and cord segmentation/area/width methods
Missing, censored and unavailable image regions
